claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's my only child.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know about Alex!

To help determine your eligibility, could you please tell me how old Alex is?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! That's helpful to know.

Could you tell me who Alex lives with? Does he live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't live with me at the moment. He lives with his dad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex lives with his dad rather than with you, I have a few more questions to understand your situation better.

Are you contributing towards the cost of looking after Alex? For example, do you pay maintenance or regularly spend money on things like clothes, food, or other essentials for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do contribute towards looking after him. I regularly help out with his clothes, school supplies, and other things he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

Could you tell me how much you contribute towards Alex's care each week? Specifically, is it at least the same amount as the current Child Benefit rate (which is £26.05 per week for the eldest or only child)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I contribute £26.05 per week towards his care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

One more important question: Is Alex's dad (or anyone else) already claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, his dad isn't claiming Child Benefit for Alex. Nobody else is claiming it for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment.

Is Alex a British citizen, or does he have the right to live in the UK? And do you live in the UK yourself?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is British and I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! That's very helpful.

One final question: Is Alex in full-time education, and does he have any approved training or employment arrangements? (At 8 years old, I assume he's in primary school, but I just want to confirm he's in full-time education.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - he's in primary school, so he's in full-time education.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm pleased to tell you that **you appear to be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why you qualify:

- ✅ **Alex's age**: At 8 years old and in full-time education, Alex meets the age requirements
- ✅ **Your contribution**: Although Alex lives with his dad, you contribute at least £26.05 per week towards his care, which meets the required threshold
- ✅ **No existing claim**: No one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- ✅ **Residency**: You live in the UK (Manchester) and Alex is a British citizen with the right to live in the UK

As the eldest (and only) child you're claiming for, Alex would qualify you for the higher rate of £26.05 per week.

You can proceed with making a claim for Child Benefit. Please note that if your individual income is over £60,000 per year, you may have to pay back some or all of the Child Benefit through the High Income Child Benefit Charge.

Is there anything else you'd like to know?
